Confidence Intervals for a Poisson Rate

Source: R/poissonCI.R
poissonCI.Rd

poissonCI() computes confidence intervals for a Poisson event rate using exact and approximate methods.

Usage

poissonCI(
  x,
  n = 1,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  sides = c("two.sided", "left", "right"),
  method = c("exact", "score", "wald", "byar")
)

Arguments

x

number of events, a non-negative integer.

n

exposure associated with x, such as observation time, person-time or population at risk; a positive number, defaults to 1.

conf.level

confidence level, defaults to 0.95.

sides

a character string specifying the side of the confidence interval, must be one of "two.sided" (default), "left" or "right". You can specify just the initial letter. sides names the side carrying the finite bound: "left" reports the lower limit and opens the upper one to Inf, "right" reports the upper limit and opens the lower one to 0. A one-sided bound at level conf.level is the corresponding end of the two-sided interval at level 2 * conf.level - 1. "left" corresponds to the alternative "greater" in a hypothesis test.

method

character string specifying which method to use; this can be one out of: "exact" (default), "score", "wald" and "byar". Several methods may be given at once; all the methods can be asked by ".all". Abbreviation of method is accepted. See details.

Value

If recycling yields a single case, a named numeric vector with elements:

est

point estimate of the event rate, x/n.

lci

lower confidence interval bound.

uci

upper confidence interval bound.

If recycling yields multiple cases, a data frame with one row per case is returned. Its first three columns are est, lci, and uci; the remaining columns contain the recycled argument values.

Details

All arguments are vectorized and recycled according to standard R rules.

The function assumes \(X \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(n\lambda)\), where \(x\) is the observed event count, \(n\) the exposure and \(\lambda\) the event rate. The point estimate is \(\hat{\lambda} = x/n\).

Exact (default): The so-called exact interval, based on quantiles of the corresponding chi-square distribution and equivalent to the Garwood (1936) interval. The same interval is returned as conf.int by poisson.test().

Score: Obtained by inverting the acceptance region of the Poisson score test.

Wald: Obtained by inverting the acceptance region of the large-sample normal (Wald) test; the interval is symmetric about \(\hat{\lambda}\).

Byar: Byar's cube-root normal approximation to the exact interval (Rothman and Boice, 1979). The lower limit is based on \(x\), the upper limit on \(x + 1\); for \(x = 0\) the lower limit is 0.

Some methods may produce a lower limit below 0. In such cases, the bound is truncated to remain within the valid parameter space \([0, \infty)\).

Which interval should be used?

The Wald interval has poor coverage for small counts and degenerates to a single point at \(x = 0\). The exact interval guarantees the nominal coverage but is conservative and often unnecessarily wide. The score interval is a good approximate alternative when conservativeness is not required.

References

Garwood, F. (1936) Fiducial limits for the Poisson distribution. Biometrika, 28, pp. 437-442.

Rothman, K. J. and Boice, J. D. Jr. (1979) Epidemiologic Analysis with a Programmable Calculator. NIH Publication No. 79-1649. Washington, DC: US Government Printing Office.

See also

poisson.test(), poissonDiffCI(), poissonRatioCI(), binomCI()

Examples


# deaths from horse kicks in 280 Prussian army corps-years
count <- 0:4
corpsYears <- c(144, 91, 32, 11, 2)

x <- sum(count * corpsYears)
n <- sum(corpsYears)

poissonCI(x, n)
#>       est       lci       uci 
#> 0.7000000 0.6054271 0.8051570 

# the exact interval corresponds to the one computed by poisson.test
poisson.test(x, n)$conf.int
#> [1] 0.6054271 0.8051570
#> attr(,"conf.level")
#> [1] 0.95

# several methods at once
poissonCI(x, n, method = c("exact", "score", "wald", "byar"))
#>   est       lci       uci   x   n conf.level     sides method
#> 1 0.7 0.6054271 0.8051570 196 280       0.95 two.sided  exact
#> 2 0.7 0.6086218 0.8050977 196 280       0.95 two.sided  score
#> 3 0.7 0.6020018 0.7979982 196 280       0.95 two.sided   wald
#> 4 0.7 0.6054225 0.8051602 196 280       0.95 two.sided   byar

# a 95% lower confidence bound for the event rate
poissonCI(x, n, sides = "left")
#>       est       lci       uci 
#> 0.7000000 0.6198372       Inf 

# SMR for Welsh nickel workers
poissonCI(x = 137, n = 24.19893)
#>      est      lci      uci 
#> 5.661407 4.753125 6.692709
